messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — want to align on query-mesh -> console SLO handshake. dashboards saw p95 spikes today when authz calls hit query service. thinking: move a small policy cache into console + optimistic fallback for reads. short sync?
Maria: ok, can you share the p95 numbers you saw?
Alex: morning spike: console p95 ~ 420ms, median ~ 80ms. query-service p95 ~ 250ms during the same interval. correlated with a burst of tenant lookups.
Sam: are these cold-cold tenant cache misses? we saw KV miss storms at 14:12 in infra logs.
Alex: yes — a handful of new tenants and some large sequence-length panel queries amplified it.
Nisha: what are users observing? full errors or degraded renders?
Alex: mostly degraded renders — placeholders and occasional 504 for heavy panels. some customers messaged success slack.
Tim: two high-level options: 1) push lightweight RBAC into console (cache + event-driven invalidation + SWR), 2) keep authoritative checks in query svc but make console render optimistically with a disabled action state until auth confirmed. tradeoffs: correctness vs latency/complexity.
Maria: console already has a small tenant token cache. adding a policy cache (policy id -> allow/deny bloom-ish) is feasible, but we need a reliable invalidation stream. we have the perm-events bus that could emit deltas. concern: memory growth and staleness window.
Sam: SRE POV: if we rely on local caches, we must track cache-miss tail and provide circuit-breakers. propose SLO targets: console p95 < 200ms, query p95 < 120ms under steady load; client timeout at 300ms so console can decide to serve stale. Also instrument 'stale_render' and 'auth_degraded' metrics.
Alex: agreed. rollout plan idea: feature-flagged canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with rollback gate. add kill-switch in console config.
Tim: implementation sketch (console config):
```yaml
feature_flags:
  auth_local_cache: on
auth_cache:
  ttl_seconds: 30
  staleness_allowed_seconds: 300
  invalidation_topic: "perm-events"
slo:
  p95_target_ms: 200
  fallback_behavior: "serve_stale_with_badge"
```
Maria: two notes: 1) invalidation topic needs consumer backpressure handling (don't let perm-events spikes OOM us), 2) we must preserve authoritative checks for mutating ops — never serve stale for write/modify actions.
Nisha: product asks that placeholders include copy: "Data is loading — showing latest cached results" and that we track user-visible degradation (ticket conversions). also add a CTA to refresh.
Alex: good call. also we should gate by panel complexity — small, cheap queries can use local cache; big multi-tenant joins should always hit query service. we'll enumerate heuristics in the RFC.
Sam: put observability hooks in: counter for cache hits/misses, histogram for stale-window served, and a tag for tenant_id to help correlation (PII-safe sampling).
Tim: agree. one more tradeoff: optimistic render reduces p95 but can hide auth regressions. we need a safety net: when auth mismatch is detected later, emit a 'consistency_violation' event and revert UI for affected widgets.
Alex: ok I'll draft an RFC with perf numbers, the event-driven invalidation design, rollout steps, and ops runbook for rollback. planning a short sync Fri 10:00am to review — @Maria @Sam @Nisha @Tim can you make it?
Maria: 👍 I'll be there.
Sam: yes, add SLO dashboards before canary.
Nisha: noted — i'll prepare product copy options.
Tim: will draft the config + eviction heuristics.
deploy-bot: meeting created: "Console auth-cache SLO sync" Fri 10:00 — calendar invite sent.
